fmt_id.evidence_quote: Germ-free mice were colonized with pre- and post-treatment stool samples from the 3 MTX-Rs with the largest decrease in Bacteroidetes

fmt_id.notes: FMT donors identified: healthy donor (Donor 1), treatment-naïve RA patients (Donors 2, 3), and 3 MTX responders with largest Bacteroidetes decrease.

fmt_role.evidence_quote: Mice were colonized with stool from human donors, either a healthy male donor or a treatment-naïve (re-MTX) female and male donors with rheumatoid arthritis
fmt_role.section: EXPERIMENTAL MODEL AND SUBJECT DETAILS — Gnotobiotic mouse studies
fmt_role.notes: Human donors provided stool samples for germ-free mouse colonization; germ-free mice served as recipients.

neonatal_birth_weight.notes: Neonatal parameters not applicable; study focuses on adult RA patients and adult-to-mouse microbiota transfer.

smoker.notes: Smoking mentioned as a factor in risk assessment but not reported as a measured variable in the study.

treatment.section: EXPERIMENTAL MODEL AND SUBJECT DETAILS — NYU Human RA patient samples acquisition
treatment.notes: Baseline RA patients (n=23) were MTX-naïve at enrollment; post-treatment samples collected 1 month after MTX initiation.

tumor_staging_ajcc.notes: AJCC tumor staging not applicable; this is a rheumatoid arthritis microbiome study, not a cancer study.

biomarker_unit.notes: Units vary by biomarker type; not all explicitly stated for each measurement

Decreased microbial richness after MTX treatment
